note: Fits the health half of the ICP and fails the commercial half, then closed at full price anyway. Neglected_health is textbook: no diagnoses, no crisis, just four or five years of not taking care of himself while working — 'I really took my hands off the reins.' Not_deconditioned is emphatic — a former college baseball player on a scholarship, in a physically demanding job, already training almost daily. Good_to_great holds on the substance if not the language: he has already restarted unaided, his sleep and mood have improved, and he is buying structure on top of momentum rather than rescue. Where he falls outside is occupation and money. Successful, as stated, means a business owner, physician or equivalent; he is a freelance touring camera operator. Income fails on his own account — no earnings since May, none until September, cost-sensitive enough to mention that he cannot afford multiple gym memberships, and he needed the payment split. This is the second clear instance in this batch, after Bennu Kham Ra Ankh Aten, of the stated ICP's commercial criteria not describing who is on the call — but with the opposite outcome, because here the deal closed at $6,000 with no discount. Read alongside the Robyn Stillwater assessment already in icp.json, which records an outside-ICP prospect closing at full price, that is now a repeating pattern rather than a one-off: the buying population is materially wider on occupation and income than the definition allows, and the criterion that actually predicted this close was the one about health being neglected rather than in crisis.
